translations.text: The life and way of living of our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Onuphrius the hermit, who completed his life on the fourteenth day of the month of Paone, in the peace of God.
Bless us. Amen.
A brother who was a hermit, named Apa Paphnutius, related this to some brothers who loved God.
These are the words he spoke: “I, your brother, thought one day of going into the inner desert to see whether there was a brother monk farther on.
I traveled for four days and four nights without eating bread or drinking water, walking through the inner desert.
On the last day, I came upon a cave.
When I approached it, I knocked at the entrance [?] for half a day, but no one answered me.
I thought to myself, ‘There is no brother in this place.’
But I saw a brother sitting there silently.
I took hold of his arm, and his arm crumbled in my hands, becoming like clods of earth.
I examined his whole body and found that he had been dead for a long time.
Then I looked and saw a tunic hanging up.
When I touched this too, it fell apart and turned to dust.
I stood up and prayed, and I took off my robe.
I wrapped it around him, dug in the ground with my hands, and buried him. Then I left that place.
I walked farther into the desert and found another cave. I took courage and called into the entrance, but no one answered me.
I went inside but found no one. I came out, saying, ‘Wherever the servant of God is, he will catch up with me here.’
I stayed in that place, praying until the day had advanced.
I was reciting the passages I had memorized.
Afterward, as the sun was about to set, I looked and saw a herd of antelopes coming from a distance, with that brother among them.
When he came close to me, he was naked. His hair covered his private parts and served as clothing to cover him.
When he reached me, he became very afraid, thinking that I was a spirit. He stood still and prayed.
For many spirits had tempted him, as he told me afterward.
When I realized that he was afraid, I walked toward him.
I said to him, ‘Why are you afraid, servant of God?
Look at my footprints and see that I am a human being. Touch me and see that I am flesh and blood.’
When he looked up, he recited the prayer from the Gospel.
I urged him to take me down into the cave.
He asked me, ‘How did you come to this place?’
I said, ‘I came here because I wanted to see the servants of God who live in this desert, and God did not deny me what I was seeking.’
I asked him, “How did you come to this place? How long has it been since you came here? What did you used to eat? And why are you naked, with no clothing on you?”
He began speaking to me, saying, “I am a monk, living in a community of monks in a monastery in the Thebaid.

A thought came into my heart: ‘Get up and leave, and find a place of your own. You will live quietly and withdraw into solitude, receive the brothers, and be very hospitable to strangers. You will also obtain a greater reward through the work of your hands.’
I did what I had thought of doing.
I left the monastery, built myself a place to live alone, and settled in it.
A number of people commissioned handiwork from me, and I used to give it as charity to strangers.
At that time the devil became jealous of the reward I was earning before the Lord for what I was doing for strangers and others in need, seeing how diligently I worked with my hands.
He became intensely jealous of me because of what I was doing. He entered a nun who used to come to me and had commissioned some handiwork from me.
When I finished the pieces, I gave them to her.
She spoke to me again about some other pieces. When meeting one another became a habit, the enemy put her into my heart, so that I would accept handiwork from her.
When we became comfortable with each other, we ate bread together.
And something developed between us. In the end, we suffered the birth pangs of death and gave birth to lawlessness.
After I foolishly had intercourse with her, we continued in this lawlessness for six months.
Afterward, I reflected in my heart on what I had done. I became frightened, wept bitterly, and fell into deep groaning.
I reflected in my heart on what I had done. I became frightened, wept bitterly, and remained in deep groaning.

I thought to myself in my heart: ‘Whether today or tomorrow, we will die, and we will be punished with severe punishments: the gnashing of teeth, the outer darkness, the unquenchable fire, and the sleepless worm that eats away at the soul.
Get up! Let us leave this place.
Let us go into the desert.’
I resolved to flee from sin.
I got up, left, and went into the wilderness.
I left behind everything belonging to that woman.
I found this spring of water, this date palm, and this cave.
This date palm produces twelve clusters of dates each year, one cluster each month.
Each month, this cluster of dates is enough for me.
I have nothing else, neither clothing nor bread to eat.
“My hair grew, and my clothes wore out completely.”
So I covered with my hair the part that ought to be covered.
It has now been thirty years since I came to this place. The air keeps my body in balance, and I have eaten no bread at all.”
I asked him, “Then how much did you suffer when you first came to this place?”

He said to me, “Oh, how much I suffered, my son! I could not throw myself to the ground because of my anguish. I could not throw myself to the ground because of my anguish, as I cried out to the Lord because of my many sins.”
“I also suffered great distress because of the [?] afflicting me.”
“I looked and saw a very glorious man standing beside me.”
“He said to me, ‘What are you suffering from?’”
“A little of my strength returned, and I said to him, ‘Sir, my liver hurts.’”
“He said to me, ‘Show me the place where you are hurting.’”
“I showed him where my liver was hurting.”
“He stretched out his hand toward me, with his fingers laid one over the other, and cut open my side as with a sword. He took out my liver and showed me the sores on it.”
“He scraped them and put their pus on a cloth. Then he put my liver back in its place.”
“He stroked my body with his hands and closed up the place he had cut open.”
“He said to me, ‘Look, you are healed. Do not return to sin, or something worse than this will happen to you. Instead, serve the Lord from now on forever.’”
“From that day onward, all my internal organs became healthy, and I stopped suffering from a liver disease.
I live in this deserted place without hardship.”
“He showed me the cloth with the pus on it.”
“I begged him to leave me in the cave where I had first seen him.”
“He said to me, ‘You do not have the strength to withstand the onslaught of the demons.’ Then I begged him to tell me his name.”
“He said to me, ‘My name is Timothy.’”
“So remember me, my beloved brother, so that the Lord may bring me to completion in the good struggle to which he called me.”
I fell at his feet, asking him to remember me and bless me.
He blessed me, saying, “May the Lord bless you and rescue you from the devil’s traps. May he keep you on all his good paths at all times, as you hurry to the saints.”
When he had finished blessing me, my strength returned, so that I felt no hunger or thirst at all.
When I saw this great miracle that had happened to me, I got up and walked farther into the mountain.
When four days had passed, I grew weary and stretched out my hands toward heaven.
I prayed, and there was the man who had come to me before.
He came to me again and strengthened me as he had the first time.
In short, the fourth day passed as I walked farther in.
Then I looked and saw a man in the distance who was very frightening. His hair spread over his body like a leopard’s, for he was naked, and leaves covered his male parts.
When he came near me, I became afraid.
I climbed onto a mountain crag, thinking that perhaps he was a mountain deer.
But when he came, he lay down for a little while in the shade of a mountain crag. He was greatly distressed by the hardships he was suffering—hunger and thirst—and was in very great danger.
He looked up at the mountain crag and saw me. He called out, “Come down to me, holy man!”
“I too am a monk like you, living in this desert because of my sins.”
He said to me, “You too are a friend of God.”
I sat down before him again and asked him to tell me his name.
He said to me, “My name is Onuphrius. Look, I have lived in this wilderness for sixty years, wandering among the mountains like the wild animals, and I have not seen anyone I knew.
“I used to live in a community of monks on the mountain of Hermopolis in the Thebaid.
The name of that plant is Erete.
“We were all of one heart with one another. There was peace among us, and we lived quietly together, giving glory to God.
“I was a young boy among them, receiving instruction from them in [?] of God. They were great men, perfect like the angels of the Lord.
“I heard them speaking about our father Elijah the Tishbite, saying how greatly he had been strengthened by God while living in this wilderness.
“And John the Baptist, among those born of women no one greater than he has arisen, lived in the wilderness until the day he appeared publicly in Israel.
“I said to them, ‘My fathers, are not those who live in the wilderness more excellent than we are?
“‘For look, we see one another every day and gather together for worship.
“‘If we are hungry, we find food prepared for us.
“‘If we are thirsty, we find water to drink.
“‘If we become weak, our brothers help us.
“‘And if we desire a dish to eat, we serve it to one another out of love for God.
“‘Where will those who live in the wilderness for God's sake find anyone if distress overtakes them?
“‘Or if they are hungry, where will they find food?
“‘If they are thirsty, where will they find water to drink?’
“For at first, when they go into solitude, they rejoice greatly because of hunger and thirst and the ways of life imposed

“by the adversary, who fights against them to tempt them through these things. He does not want them to remain in solitude, knowing that the reward they will receive from God when they leave the body is great.
“As soon as they endure, God's mercy reaches them. He makes the angels serve them their food and brings them water out of a rock.
“For it is written in Isaiah, ‘Those who wait patiently for the Lord will renew their strength.’”
They will grow wings like eagles.
They will run and not fall.
They will walk and not grow hungry.
He said, “Water will be brought out of a rock for them.”
And again, when they are hungry, he makes the plants in the field taste sweet in their mouths, like sweet honey.

If distress overtakes them or danger rises against them, they immediately stretch out their hands and pray to King Jesus until his help quickly reaches them, and he immediately sends them forth and strengthens them because their hearts are upright toward him.
Have you not heard what is written: “The Lord will not abandon his people,” and, “The patience of the needy will not perish forever”?
And again: “The poor man cried out.”
The Lord heard him.
He saved him from all his troubles.
God gives to each person according to the hardship that he will endure.
Blessed is the one who will do God's will on earth.
I tell you that the angels will serve him even while he is in the body, and they will keep comforting him at all times in his needs.
As for me, brother, when I heard these things from these perfected men of God, they became like sweet honey in my heart.
And a great awareness arose within me.
I became like those whose minds have moved into the other age.
I got up immediately.
I took a few loaves of bread with me, enough for four days of walking, so that I could eat them until I reached the place the Lord would appoint for me.
When I came out of my monastery, I looked.
I saw a light before me.
I was afraid.
I thought in my heart of turning back to the place where I had been before and remaining as I had been.
When he realized that I was afraid, he said to me, “Do not be afraid.”
“I am the angel assigned to you, who has walked with you since your childhood.”
“This mission that the Lord has assigned to you—you will [?] complete it.”
When I went into the mountain, I walked through the desert for a good seven miles.
I saw a cave.
I bent down over it to see whether anyone was inside.
A great holy man of God came out to me, beautiful in appearance, with great grace upon his face.
When I saw him, I bowed down before him.
But he raised me up.
He greeted me.
He said to me, “You are Onuphrius, my fellow worker in the Lord.
Come inside.
The Lord is with you. May you succeed in the good work to which he has called you.”
I went inside.
I stayed with him for a few days.
I received instruction from him in building up godliness.
And he taught me how to work in the desert.

When he saw that I understood the hidden warfare and the terrors that exist in the desert, he said to me, “Get up, my son, and let us go. I will take you to a deserted place in the inner wilderness, so that you may live there alone for God's sake.
For the Lord God has appointed you to this work, to live in the desert.”
Immediately he got up and walked with me into the desert, a journey of four days.
At the end of four days, we came upon a small hut.
He said to me, “This is the place the Lord has appointed for you to live in.”
He stayed with me for a month, until I understood the good work that I ought to do.
Afterward he went away from me.
And we would see one another once a year, until the day he laid down his body.
And I buried him in the place where he lived.
I said to him, “My beloved, good father, when you first came to this place, did you suffer from the start?”
The blessed old man said to me, “How much I suffered, many times, because of hunger and thirst, and because of the burning heat outside during the day and the severe cold at night!
My flesh wasted away from the dew of the sky.

But when God [?] that I had persevered in the good struggle of fasting and had devoted my heart to ascetic discipline, he made the holy angels serve me my daily food, giving it to me at night and sustaining my body.
The palm tree produced twelve clusters of dates for me each year, and I ate one cluster each month.
He also made the other plants growing on the mountain taste sweet in my mouth, like honey.
For it is written: “A person will not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God; a person will live on these.”
If you do God's will, he will take care of you everywhere.
For he said in the holy Gospel, “Do not worry about what you will eat, what you will drink, or what you will wear. Your Father in heaven knows what you need before you ask him.”
Rather, seek his kingdom and his righteousness.
And these things will be added to you.
When I heard these things, I was greatly amazed. I said to him, “My holy father, where do you receive communion on Saturday and Sunday?”
He said to me, “My holy father,
an angel of God comes and gives me communion on Saturday and Sunday. And everyone who is in the desert, living for God's sake and not [?] people—
an angel comes, gives them communion, and comforts them.

And if they desire to see people, they are taken up into heaven, where they see all the saints and greet them. Their hearts are enlightened, and they rejoice and delight with God in the good things there.
When they see them, they are comforted and forget that they have suffered at all. Afterward they return to their bodies and remain comforted for a long time.
If they have passed into the other age through the joy they have seen, they do not even remember that a world exists.”
When I heard this, I rejoiced greatly because I had been found worthy to hear these things from him.
And I forgot all the hardships I had suffered while traveling through the mountains.
Strength came into my body.
And renewal came into my body and my soul.
I said to him, “Blessed am I, because I have been worthy to see your holy face and worthy to hear your sweet words.”
Then he said to me, “Get up, my brother, and let us go to the place where we stay.”
We got up.
We walked together for two or three miles. The marvelous character of this blessed old man and spiritual athlete was truly astonishing. As we walked, we came upon a hut.
When we entered the hut, he stood up and prayed with me.
When we finished the prayer, we said “Amen.”
Then we sat down together.
We continued talking about God's greatness.
And when the sun was about to set, I looked
and saw a loaf of bread lying there, along with a vessel of water.
He said to me, “Get up, my brother, and eat, and drink this little water, for I see that you are in danger from hunger, thirst, and the hardships of the journey.”
But I said to him, “As God Almighty lives, I will neither eat nor drink until we recline and eat together.”
After I kept insisting, we finally reclined together.
We broke the bread.
We ate.
We left some of it.
We also both drank from the vessel of water.
We drank, and we left some of it.
And we spent the whole night praying to God until dawn.
When dawn came, I saw that his face had changed.
It had altered so that he looked like another person.
He became entirely like fire.
And his appearance frightened me greatly.
But he said to me, “Do not be afraid, my brother Paphnutius, for the Lord sent you to care for my body and bury it.
For today I will finish my appointed task and go to the place of rest forever.”
For that day was the sixteenth of the month of Paone.
He said to me again, “When you go to Egypt, tell others about me as an encouragement to the brothers.
“Whoever gives an offering in my name to commemorate me, Jesus himself will bring him in at the first hour of the thousand years.”
But I said to him, “What if he is poor and cannot give an offering in your name?”
He said to me, “Let him feed a poor brother in my name.”
He said to me, “If he is poor and cannot feed him, will you not bring him to the banquet at the first hour of the thousand years?”
He said to me, “Let him offer a little incense in my name.”
But I said to him, “What if he is poor and cannot offer incense in your name because of his poverty?
Yes, my good father, may your mercy reach us all, for whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”
He said to me, “Let him stand up and pray to God three times in my name, and the Lord Jesus will bring him into the thousand years, and he will share in the inheritance with all the saints.”
But I said to him, “O my holy father, if I am worthy, I wish to remain in your holy place when you leave this body.”
He said to me, “Do not, my son.

For you were not appointed to this service by people. Rather, the Lord appointed you to comfort the holy brothers who live in the desert, so that you might tell about them and their encouragement among the brothers who serve God, for the benefit of those who hear.”
Go away to Egypt, my son, and continue doing good work.”
Immediately I fell down on the ground.

I said to him, “Bless me, my father, so that I may receive mercy from God. Just as I was worthy to see you on earth, may I also be worthy to see you in the world to come, beside the Lord Jesus Christ.”

But he said to me, “My son, God will not cause you sorrow in anything. He will strengthen you in his love, and your eyes will receive light through his divinity. You will neither falter nor fall, but you will succeed in the work you have undertaken.”
May the angels protect you and rescue you from the plots of the Jews, so that they find no accusation against you when you meet God.
When he had finished saying these things, he stood up.
He prayed to God with sighs and many tears.
Afterward, he lay down on the ground.
He completed his service to God and gave his spirit into God's hands on the twelfth day of the month of Paone.
I heard the voices of angels singing hymns before the blessed Apa Onuphrius. There was great joy as he went to meet God.
I stripped off the tunic I was wearing.
I gave half of it for the burial, and I covered myself with the other half so that I would not remain naked.
I laid his body down in a cleft in a rock.
I heard the sound of a multitude of angels rejoicing and crying out, “Hallelujah!”
I offered my prayer over him and piled many stones over him.
I stood up.
I prayed a second time, and immediately the palm tree fell.
I was greatly amazed at what had happened.
I ate the bread that was left and drank the water that had been left for us.
When I saw that it was not God's will for me to stay in this place, I stretched out my hands.
I prayed to the Lord. And look, the man who had come to me at first strengthened me. He came to me again as he had the first time.
He said to me, “Paphnutius, our Lord told us today that you were coming to us here.
For sixty years we have seen no human being except you alone.”
When we had spent some time talking with one another,
Then we said to him, “Our brother, strengthen your heart with a little bread, because you have come a long way.
The Lord has appointed us to stay together for one day.
We rejoice with you, our beloved brother.”
While we were speaking with one another, look, five loaves were brought in, hot and fresh, as though they had just been baked in the oven.
Immediately, something else to eat was also brought in.
We sat down and ate together.
And he said to me, “This is the sixth year since we came to this place.
Four loaves of bread are allotted to us each day, and they are brought to us by God.
But when you came to us today, look, your portion was brought for you.”
and we never knew where they had come from, but we would come in and find them lying there.
When we had finished eating together, we spent the whole night praying until dawn.
When dawn came, I begged them to let me stay with them until the day of my death.
They said to me, “Our brother, it has not been ordained for you to stay here.
Instead, get up and go to Egypt, and tell the brothers what you have seen, as a reminder to them and for the benefit of those who hear.”
I begged them to tell me their names, but they were unwilling to say them.
I pressed them, but still they did not tell me their names.
They answered, saying, “The one who gave a name to everything and knows everything is the one who knows our names.
Now then, our brother, remember us until we see you in the house of God.
Be diligent, and do not let the world enslave you, for it has enslaved many.”
When they had finished saying these things, they blessed me and embraced me.
I departed from them.
When I was a day's journey away from them, I came upon a spring of water.
I sat down for a little while because I was tired, and there were large trees growing beside the spring.
After I had lain down and rested a little, I continued looking at the trees in amazement.
And I wondered who had planted them in this place.
Among them were also date palms laden with fruit, citron trees, pomegranate trees, fig trees, apple trees, grapevines, peach trees, [?], and other trees giving off a sweet fragrance.
The spring poured out water, watering all the trees growing in that place.
While I was marveling at the trees and looking at them and their fruit, four young boys came from a distance. They were beautiful in appearance and wore beautiful palm leaves like loincloths.
When they reached me, they said to me, “Greetings, Paphnutius, our beloved brother!”
I bowed down.
I paid homage to them.
But they raised me up.
They greeted me.
They were in great peace, like people who had passed into the next world, in their joy and the comfort they offered me.
They kept picking fruit from the trees and putting it into my mouth.
My heart rejoiced because of the kindness they showed me.
For I spent seven days with them, eating the fruit of the trees.
I asked them, “Where did you come from to this place, and where are you from?”
They said to him, “Our brother, God has sent you to us. We will tell you about our whole life.
We are from a city in Egypt called Oxyrhynchus.
Our fathers were members of the city council, and they sent us to school to be educated.
We were together in the same school, and we were of one heart.
After we had been educated in the school, they sent us to the [?], after they had educated us
well, with all diligence and all the wisdom of this world. But now we wanted to be educated in the wisdom of God.
One day, as we were discussing these things with one another, a good thought began to work within our inner selves.
The four of us got up.
We went into the mountains to live in solitude until we could see what the Lord would decide.
We took some small loaves with us, enough for seven days.
When we had gone far into the mountains, a trance immediately came upon us.
A man who was entirely light took us by the hand.
He brought us to this place.
When we came to this place, we found a holy man of God, and the angel of the Lord entrusted us to him.
He continued teaching us to serve God for a full year.
At the end of the year, the holy and blessed old man passed away.
We alone are the ones living in this place, our lord and brother.
Look, we solemnly declare to you by the Lord that for sixty years we have known neither the taste of bread nor any other food except these trees alone, living on their fruit.

For when we want to see one another, we come to this place every week to see one another, and we spend the whole night of the Lord’s Day together. Afterward, each one goes away to continue his way of life.”
I said to them, “Where do you receive communion?”
They said to me, “We gather here for this purpose, because every Sabbath an angel of God comes and gives us communion on the Sabbath and on the Lord’s Day.”
I stayed with them, rejoicing greatly.
“On the seventh day an angel of the Lord comes and gives us communion together with you.
Anyone who receives communion through that angel will be cleansed of every sin, and no adversary will be able to overpower him.”
While we were speaking with one another, I smelled a powerful fragrance. I had never smelled anything like it.
As soon as the fragrance reached us, we rose, stood up, and praised God.
Afterward an angel came.
He gave us communion together in the body and blood of the Lord.
I became like someone in a trance because of the terrifying sight I had seen.
He blessed us.
He went up to heaven while we watched him with our own eyes.
After he had gone, they brought me back to my senses.
They said to me, “Be firm, take courage, and be a strong man.”
Immediately I became sober, like those who are drunk on wine.
We spent the whole night of the Lord’s Day standing in prayer until dawn.
When the light rose early on the Lord’s Day, once again we smelled that sweet fragrance.
We took delight in it and [?] rejoiced like those in the age to come.
Afterward the angel came.
He gave us communion and blessed each one of us, saying, “May it be eternal life for you and an imperishable prophecy.”
All of us together answered with one voice, “Amen. May it be so.”
Afterward the angel turned toward me.
He said to me, “Get up and set out for Egypt. Tell the brothers who love God what you have seen, so that they may strive to follow the way of life of the saints.”
I begged him to let me stay with them.
He said to me, “The Lord has not assigned us work for us to work in the same way. Rather, God gives each person according to what he can bear.
So now get up and go, for this is what he has appointed for you.”
And he blessed me.
He went to heaven in glory.
And they brought a large amount of fruit.
We ate together.
And I left them, and they accompanied me for six miles.
And I asked them, “Tell me your names.”
And they told me their names one by one.
The first was John.
The second was Andrew.
The third was Heraclammon.
The fourth was Theophilus.
And they instructed me to tell their names to the brothers so that they would remember them.
And I, in turn, begged them to remember me.
We prayed and greeted one another.
I went away deeply saddened.
But I was rejoicing because of the blessing the holy men had given me.
And I came out to Egypt by a route that took three days of walking.
And when I found the God-loving brothers, I rested with them for ten days.
And I told them what had happened to me.
And they said, “Truly, you have been found worthy of a great gift of grace.”
For the brothers there loved God and were ascetics who served God with all their hearts, and their dwelling place was Scetis.
And they hurried to write down these words that they had heard from Father Paphnutius.
They quickly put them into a book.
They sent it to Scetis.
They placed it in the church for the benefit of those who would hear it.
And they spoke about him; he was a subject for reflection on everyone’s lips.

They glorified God and blessed his saints through the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom glory belongs to him, together with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, forever and ever.
Amen.
I, Victor, the lowliest deacon, son of the blessed Mercurius, deacon of Saint Mercurius the great commander, from the city of Latopolis, wrote the book.
Remember me, Lord, when—Greek—you come into your kingdom.
It was written on the third of the month of Tybi, in year 721 of the holy martyrs, in year 365, in the third indiction.

Through the diligence and care of our fathers and beloved brothers: Abba Abraham, the superior of [?]; the archdeacon Abba Chael; and the deputy Zechariah, the deacon and monk of the monastery of Saint Mercurius the commander, which is on the mountain of Edfu.
They produced this book through their own labors.

They placed it in their monastery so that it would be read there, for the benefit and assurance of those who would read it and anyone who would listen to it attentively, so that our good Savior and Saint Apa Onuphrius the hermit would bless them and the entire community of their monastery with the blessing of heaven and the blessing of the earth in all fullness.
And may he establish lasting blessing, abundance, peace, and salvation in their monastery.
And may he save them from the snares of the devil and from wicked people.

And when they leave the body, according to what is appointed for everyone, may they hear: “Well done, good and faithful servant! Since you have been faithful over a few things, I will put you in charge of many. Enter into the joy of your Lord.”
And may they be worthy to receive an inheritance with all the saints. Amen. So be it.
